subject: Service impact: FlowBase - elevated 5xx/429 and throughput loss
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.t@flowbase.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: sre-oncall@flowbase.com
Date: 2025-06-30T02:14:00Z
Subject: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out

Sean —

Starting ~01:50 UTC we're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your API for our production tenant (tenant_id: fb-prod-17). Throughput dropped ~70% and our clients are experiencing timeouts. We've attached a short sample of error traces and client retry logs.

Key impact: many of our end-users are seeing degraded search and ingestion flows. Our SRE team has already started emergency rate-limiting on the client side but the retry storm is making things worse. Can you confirm whether this is on your side or a cloud provider network issue? This is severely impacting our SLAs — please escalate.

Attachments: flowbase_error_sample.log (text), client-retry-snippets.txt (text)

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Platform
FlowBase
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.t@flowbase.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T02:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out

Alex — thank you for the alert and the logs. I’ve opened a high-priority incident on our side and looped in SRE, product and CS. We’re treating this as a Sev1. Immediate next steps:
- Paging infra on-call and starting a live incident bridge (PD INC123456).
- Collecting full request/response metrics and tracing for fb-prod-17.
- Applying conservative per-tenant throttles to limit retry amplification.

Can you confirm whether you’ve applied any backoff on the client side and share any additional traces? We’ll post continuous updates to this thread and the PD incident.

Apologies for the impact — we’re on it.

Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T03:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out

Quick update from infra metrics (us-west-2 cluster):
- From 01:45–02:15 UTC we see a sudden jump in 429 and 5xx across front-end gateways for several tenants; fb-prod-17 is the worst hit.
- Correlation found with increased Route53 latency and a burst of ENI detach/reattach errors on a subset of hosts (AWS notice: networking flap in us-west-2).
- Autoscaling added workers but errors did not drop — symptoms of retry amplification and upstream DNS latency causing timeouts/retries to pile up.

Short-term mitigations executed (03:00 UTC):
- Applied per-tenant dynamic throttling for fb-prod-17 to cap concurrency and reduce retry amplification.
- Disabled aggressive prefix batching for that tenant to reduce tail latency.
- Switched routing for a portion of production traffic to a secondary region for critical endpoints (read-only paths).

We’ve attached a packet capture and response-time CSV with request-level breakdowns. Next: coordinate with AWS support and our DNS provider to confirm root cause and mitigation timeline.

Attachments: netdiag-trace.pcap, response-metrics-20250630.csv

Rishi
Head of Infra, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.t@flowbase.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T05:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out

Alex — thank you for staying patient. To summarize what we’ve done so far and the plan:

1) Stabilization (complete): dynamic throttles for fb-prod-17; partial traffic failover to secondary region for read endpoints.
2) Investigation (in progress): AWS confirmed a networking disruption in us-west-2 that impacted ENI reliability and Route53 resolution latency; our engineering team validated that the spike amplified due to client retries.
3) Mitigations (next 24h): permanent per-tenant concurrency controls, improved client-side retry guidance, and a short-term credit for the incident.

We’re proposing a one-time SLA credit per the contract while we finish the RCA. Would you be OK with a 7-day credit for affected usage while we complete the full postmortem?

We’ll continue to update you via this thread and the PD incident.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Torres <alex.t@flowbase.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T07:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick response and mitigations. We have applied client-side backoff and are seeing fewer retries, traffic looks more stable. A couple items:
- Please confirm the credit and provide expected timeline for RCA (we need it for our internal postmortem).
- We need an exact list of affected endpoints and time windows to reconcile our monitoring.

Alex
Head of Platform, FlowBase
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T09:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Major spike in 5xx/429 - apps timing out (exec summary for leadership)

Evelyn — forwarding the incident thread for visibility and any executive outreach. Short exec summary below for leadership distribution: 

- Impact: FlowBase (fb-prod-17) experienced a ~70% throughput drop and elevated 5xx/429 between ~01:45–03:30 UTC on 2025-06-30 due to an AWS us-west-2 networking disruption that increased DNS and connection timeouts; client retry storms amplified the effect.
- Mitigation: dynamic per-tenant throttles, temporary routing to secondary region for read endpoints, and conservative batching changes. Stabilized by 05:00 UTC; traffic restored to baseline by ~06:15 UTC.
- Customer action: FlowBase applied client backoff and confirmed improved stability.
- Proposed customer-facing actions: issue a 7-day usage credit, deliver full RCA within 5 business days, and publish a best-practice note for retry/backoff behavior.

Primary ask: approval to proceed with the proposed credit and to authorize a short executive note to the FlowBase CEO if you think it’s warranted.

Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
